WinUI theme: window tiers

The thresholds follow NavigationView’s own defaults (CompactModeThresholdWidth 641, ExpandedModeThresholdWidth 1008), plus 1920 for Huge. Widths are effective pixels. Every change animates or keeps its space reserved. Nothing snaps. When the window gets narrower, each threshold waits 24 px longer before switching, so dragging back and forth over a line doesn’t flicker.

Title bar: tabs stay on in every tier

Compact, 400: the selected tab keeps its label (140); the others become 36 px icon tabs; Search becomes a button
Compact, tabs Off: no strip. One 48 px bar holds the caption buttons; the other tabs stay open in the background (Q4)
Small, 800: tabs 160 → down to 110, then the strip scrolls. Pin and Friends move into ⋯. Search fills the middle (max 520)
Small, tabs Off: the Wavee mark sits after Back/Forward, and the caption buttons end the bar
Standard keeps 200 px tabs and a 520 search. Huge uses 240 px tabs, a 640 search and shows the profile name. With tabs Off in any tier, the window shows one page: Ctrl+T opens a new page in the background, Ctrl+Tab still cycles, and turning tabs back on restores the strip with every tab in place.

{{p.k}} {{c.v}}
Medium · 860–1099: shuffle and repeat return; Lyrics and Queue return; volume stays a button with a flyout slider
Full · 1100–1919: the volume slider and Full screen return (the Standard boards’ bar). Huge adds a 720 seek column, a labelled “This PC” device button and a 128 slider
Order of collapse as the window narrows: volume slider → Full screen → Lyrics, Queue → Shuffle, Repeat → Previous, seek bar (Mini). The ⋯ menu always lists what the bar no longer shows, in the same order, so a control never disappears. The like heart, Play/Pause and Next never collapse. The bar’s height (72) is reserved in every tier except Mini (64). The change between them animates over 167 ms.
